Get the up-to-date/first/last mode or first/last entry from a vector

Source: R/get_ultimate.R
get_ultimate.Rd

This function finds the most recent (i.e., up-to-date) mode, the first/last mode, or the first/last entry from a vector, with options to ignore specific values. Particularly useful for finding the most current valid values in longitudinal data. NA values are excluded by default (na.rm = TRUE); set na.rm = FALSE when a missing value is meaningful and should be considered like any other value.

Usage

get_ultimate(x, find, exclude = NULL, warn = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE)

Arguments

x

A vector of values to be evaluated. Can be numeric, character, but date (POSIXct) is currently not supported.

find

Character string specifying what to find. Options are:

  • "uptodate_mode" - Among all modal values, returns the one that appears last in the vector

  • "first_mode" - Among all modal values, returns the first mode in order of unique values

  • "last_mode" - Among all modal values, returns the last mode in order of unique values

  • "first_entry" - The first valid entry in the vector (after exclusions)

  • "last_entry" - The last valid entry in the vector (after exclusions)

exclude

A value or vector of values to ignore/exclude from consideration. Can be a single value (e.g., 99, "Unknown") or multiple values (e.g., c(99, "Unknown")). Must not contain NA (an error is thrown); use na.rm to control how NAs are handled. Default is NULL (nothing is excluded).

warn

Logical. Whether to display warning messages. Warnings are shown when multiple modal values exist, showing the remaining modes apart from the one designated in find, or when x contains NAs and na.rm is not specified (they are removed by default). Default is TRUE.

na.rm

Logical. Whether to exclude NAs before evaluating. Default is TRUE. If FALSE, NA will be considered as a valid candidate and treated like any other value.

Value

The result based on the find, exclude and na.rm parameters. If no valid values remain after exclusions, returns NA. With na.rm = FALSE, NA is also returned when it is itself the selected mode or entry. When multiple modes exist and warn = TRUE, a warning message lists the other modal values not returned.

Examples

# Example 1: Exclude invalid entries before finding the designated value
x <- c(1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 1, 99, 99, 99, 99, NA, NA, NA, NA)
get_ultimate(x, find = "uptodate_mode")  # 99
#> Warning: NAs are removed by default with `na.rm = TRUE`
#> [1] 99
get_ultimate(x, find = "uptodate_mode",
             exclude = 99)               # 1, NAs excluded by default
#> Warning: NAs are removed by default with `na.rm = TRUE`
#> Warning: There are multiple modes, the remaining modes are: 2
#> [1] 1
get_ultimate(x, find = "uptodate_mode",
             exclude = 99, na.rm=FALSE)      # NA, if NAs are meaningful
#> [1] NA
# When all values are excluded
x <- c(99, 99, 99, 99, NA, NA, NA, NA)
get_ultimate(x, find = 'uptodate_mode')  # 99 (BAD PRACTICE)
#> Warning: NAs are removed by default with `na.rm = TRUE`
#> [1] 99
get_ultimate(x, find = 'uptodate_mode',
             exclude = 99)               # NA (GOOD PRACTICE)
#> Warning: NAs are removed by default with `na.rm = TRUE`
#> [1] NA
get_ultimate(c(9,9,9,9,9), find='uptodate_mode',
             exclude = 9, warn = FALSE)        # NA
#> [1] NA
get_ultimate(c(9,9,9,9,9), find='last_entry',
             exclude = 9, warn = FALSE)        # NA
#> [1] NA

# Example 2: Finding up-to-date mode with categorical data
x <- c("F", "F", "Other", "Other", "Unknown",
        "Other", "M", "M", "M", "M", "F", "F",
        "Other", "Unknown", "Unknown", "Unknown")
get_ultimate(x, find = "uptodate_mode",
             exclude = "Unknown")       # "Other" (last occurrence) (GOOD)
#> Warning: There are multiple modes, the remaining modes are: F, M
#> [1] "Other"
get_ultimate(x, find = "uptodate_mode") # "Unknown" (BAD)
#> Warning: There are multiple modes, the remaining modes are: F, Other, M
#> [1] "Unknown"
get_ultimate(x, find = "first_mode",
             warn = FALSE)              # "F" (first among unique modes)
#> [1] "F"
get_ultimate(x, find = "last_mode",
             warn = FALSE)           # "M" (last among unique modes)
#> [1] "M"

# Example 3: Finding first/last valid entry
get_ultimate(x, find = "last_entry",
             warn = FALSE)           # "Unknown" (BAD)
#> [1] "Unknown"
get_ultimate(x, find = "last_entry", exclude = "Unknown",
             warn = FALSE)           # "Other" (GOOD)
#> [1] "Other"
get_ultimate(x, find = "first_entry", exclude = "Unknown",
             warn = FALSE)           # "F"
#> [1] "F"
